   "source": [
    "## Sanity checking when model behaviours should overlap\n",
    "\n",
    "Many of the model classes in GPflow have overlapping behaviour in special cases. In this notebook, we fit some approximations to a model with a Gaussian likelihood, and make sure they're all the same.\n",
    "\n",
    "The models are:\n",
    " - `GPR`: Full Gaussian process regression.\n",
    "\n",
    " - `VGP`: A Gaussian approximation with Variational Bayes.\n",
    "   Approximating a Gaussian posterior with a Gaussian should be exact.\n",
    "\n",
    " - `SVGP`: a sparse GP, with a Gaussian approximation. The inducing points are set to be at the data points, so again, should be exact.\n",
    "\n",
    " - `SVGP` (with whitened representation): As above, but with a rotation applied to whiten the representation of the process.\n",
    "\n",
    " - `SGPR`: A sparse GP with a *collapsed* posterior (Titsias 2009). Again, the inducing points are fixed to the data points.\n",
    "\n",
    " - `GPRFITC`: The FITC approximation. Again, the inducing points are fixed to the data points.\n",
    "\n",
    "In all cases the parameters are estimated by the method of maximum likelihood (or approximate maximum likelihood, as appropriate). The parameter estimates should all be the same."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "da5572ea",

    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import tensorflow as tf\n",
    "\n",
    "import gpflow\n",
    "from gpflow import set_trainable\n",
    "from gpflow.ci_utils import reduce_in_tests\n",
    "from gpflow.config import default_float\n",
    "from gpflow.models import (\n",
    "    maximum_log_likelihood_objective,\n",
    "    training_loss_closure,\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "%matplotlib inline\n",
    "plt.rcParams[\"figure.figsize\"] = (12, 6)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "dd0368db",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-15T09:27:19.509513Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-15T09:27:19.509161Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-15T09:27:19.631056Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-15T09:27:19.630378Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 1200x600 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "np.random.seed(0)\n",
    "X = np.random.rand(20, 1) * 10\n",
    "Y = np.sin(X) + 0.9 * np.cos(X * 1.6) + np.random.randn(*X.shape) * 0.4\n",
    "Xtest = np.random.rand(10, 1) * 10\n",
    "plt.plot(X, Y, \"kx\", mew=2)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "id": "31c320c1",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-15T09:27:19.632670Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-15T09:27:19.632501Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-15T09:27:19.868877Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-15T09:27:19.868200Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stderr",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "2026-10-15 09:27:19.636749: E external/local_xla/xla/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:152] failed call to cuInit: INTERNAL: CUDA error: Failed call to cuInit: UNKNOWN ERROR (303)\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "data = (\n",
    "    tf.convert_to_tensor(X, dtype=default_float()),\n",
    "    tf.convert_to_tensor(Y, dtype=default_float()),\n",
    ")\n",
    "inducing_variable = tf.convert_to_tensor(X, dtype=default_float())\n",
    "\n",
    "m1 = gpflow.models.GPR(data, kernel=gpflow.kernels.SquaredExponential())\n",
    "m2 = gpflow.models.VGP(\n",
    "    data,\n",
    "    kernel=gpflow.kernels.SquaredExponential(),\n",
    "    likelihood=gpflow.likelihoods.Gaussian(),\n",
    ")\n",
    "m3 = gpflow.models.SVGP(\n",
    "    gpflow.kernels.SquaredExponential(),\n",
    "    gpflow.likelihoods.Gaussian(),\n",
    "    inducing_variable,\n",
    "    q_diag=False,\n",
    ")\n",
    "set_trainable(m3.inducing_variable, False)\n",
    "\n",
    "m4 = gpflow.models.SVGP(\n",
    "    gpflow.kernels.SquaredExponential(),\n",
    "    gpflow.likelihoods.Gaussian(),\n",
    "    inducing_variable,\n",
    "    q_diag=False,\n",
    "    whiten=True,\n",
    ")\n",
    "set_trainable(m4.inducing_variable, False)\n",
    "\n",
    "m5 = gpflow.models.SGPR(\n",
    "    data,\n",
    "    kernel=gpflow.kernels.SquaredExponential(),\n",
    "    inducing_variable=inducing_variable,\n",
    ")\n",
    "set_trainable(m5.inducing_variable, False)\n",
    "\n",
    "m6 = gpflow.models.GPRFITC(\n",
    "    data,\n",
    "    kernel=gpflow.kernels.SquaredExponential(),\n",
    "    inducing_variable=inducing_variable,\n",
    ")\n",
    "set_trainable(m6.inducing_variable, False)\n",
    "\n",
    "models = [m1, m2, m3, m4, m5, m6]"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "0bfbf973",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Now, we optimize the models. For `GPR`, `SVGP`, and `GPRFITC`, this simply optimizes the hyperparameters (since the inducing points are fixed). For the variational models, this jointly maximises the lower bound to the marginal likelihood (Evidence Lower Bound, ELBO) with respect to the variational parameters and the kernel and likelihood hyperparameters."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "id": "478efa95",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-15T09:27:19.870886Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-15T09:27:19.870710Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-15T09:27:27.739141Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-15T09:27:27.738252Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "for m in models:\n",
    "    opt = gpflow.optimizers.Scipy()\n",
    "    loss_closure = training_loss_closure(m, data)\n",
    "    opt.minimize(\n",
    "        loss_closure,\n",
    "        variables=m.trainable_variables,\n",
    "        options=dict(maxiter=reduce_in_tests(1000)),\n",
    "        compile=True,\n",
    "    )"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "680f1ff3",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "If everything worked as planned, the models should have the same:\n",
    "\n",
    " - prediction functions\n",
    " - log (marginal) likelihood\n",
    " - kernel parameters\n",
    "\n",
    "For the variational models, where we use a ELBO in place of the likelihood, the ELBO should be tight to the likelihood in the cases studied here."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "42c15e4a",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-15T09:27:27.741036Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-15T09:27:27.740832Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-15T09:27:28.345396Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-15T09:27:28.344587Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",

       "<Figure size 1200x900 with 6 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "def plot(m, color, ax):\n",
    "    xx = np.linspace(-1, 11, 100)[:, None]\n",
    "    mu, var = m.predict_y(xx)\n",
    "    ax.plot(xx, mu, color, lw=2)\n",
    "    ax.fill_between(\n",
    "        xx[:, 0],\n",
    "        mu[:, 0] - 2 * np.sqrt(var[:, 0]),\n",
    "        mu[:, 0] + 2 * np.sqrt(var[:, 0]),\n",
    "        color=color,\n",
    "        alpha=0.2,\n",
    "    )\n",
    "    ax.plot(X, Y, \"kx\", mew=2)\n",
    "    ax.set_xlim(-1, 11)\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "f, ax = plt.subplots(3, 2, sharex=True, sharey=True, figsize=(12, 9))\n",
    "plot(m1, \"C0\", ax[0, 0])\n",
    "plot(m2, \"C1\", ax[1, 0])\n",
    "plot(m3, \"C2\", ax[0, 1])\n",
    "plot(m4, \"C3\", ax[1, 1])\n",
    "plot(m5, \"C4\", ax[2, 0])\n",
    "plot(m6, \"C5\", ax[2, 1])"
   ]
  },
  {

   "metadata": {},
